output.brief: The buffering is not coming from the new CDN. Tessaline serves every Kestria client, and the 5.9% rebuffering is confined to smart-TV app 5.2, across all three ISPs. Web, iOS/Android, and smart-TV 5.1 on auto-update-off devices stay at about 0.6–0.7%, the same as before the move. The rise also began at the 9 October cutover, the same day app 5.2 went live, and two days before the handball launch. The handball and ISP congestion explanations do not fit that pattern. The CDN move is the wrong target. Do not send the SLA notice, withhold fees, or move traffic back. Those steps would penalise a vendor that is not the cause and would not fix the problem. Silencing the alert would hide an ongoing fault. The better next step is to roll back or hold the 5.2 adaptive-streaming settings for Kestria to 5.1 and confirm the effect on the dashboard. Confidence is moderate: I have not checked the release configuration itself, so the mechanism is inferred from the pattern, not yet confirmed. The per-app breakdown also needs a pipeline change that takes about six weeks, so I could not monitor this with the dashboard in the meantime.
